source.title: Orthogonal Over-Parameterized Training
source.authors: Wei-Yang Liu; Rongmei Lin; Zhen Liu; J. Rehg; Liam Paull; Li Xiong; Le Song; Adrian Weller

record.file_problem: None; full paper and appendix text supplied.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares a different training procedure, orthogonal over-parameterized training (OPT), with standard training and reports test performance. It does not test the specific interventions or measurements defined in V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test error and accuracy for OPT variants and baselines, and test-error landscapes under parameter perturbations. It does not report random-label fitting, interpolation-threshold width sweeps, convolution-versus-fully-connected comparisons, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Results cited from prior work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates OPT against standard training, but its own results do not test V1–V8. Its landscape visualizations concern perturbation sensitivity under different parameterizations, without measuring the magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap relationship in V7. Reporting improved test performance alone does not test these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors claim that OPT preserves low hyperspherical energy and improves empirical generalization across diverse evaluated tasks, while explicitly leaving a rigorous proof of better generalization to future work. This should not imply every variant improves every result: CLS-OPT sacrifices accuracy in several parameter-saving comparisons.
record.recipe_differences: OPT fixes randomly initialized neuron weights and learns shared orthogonal transformations; the study compares this training framework with standard training and other OPT parameterizations.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary across orthogonalization methods, network architectures, neuron-weight normalization, and whether BatchNorm is used; the paper also reports different accuracy and parameter counts as S-OPT sampling dimension changes.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-100, OPT variants lower test error relative to standard training: CNN-6 gives 33.02–35.67% versus 37.59%, and CNN-9 gives 31.03–32.75% versus 33.55%. Normalization and orthogonality choices affect performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Orthogonal reparameterization of fixed random neuron weights can improve held-out performance relative to the reported standard-training baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors describe smoother training-loss landscapes and slower increases in testing error under perturbations for OPT. Baseline weights and OPT trainable matrices are perturbed in different parameterizations; no sharpness-to-generalization-gap ranking is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: OPT's trainable parameterization can yield smoother plotted landscapes and greater testing-error robustness to the sampled perturbations than standard training.

record.problems: Most experiments report averages over 10 runs but no uncertainty estimates. Comparisons generally report test performance and do not show whether training error is matched or near zero. The landscape findings are qualitative and figure-based; the perturbation parameterizations differ between baseline and OPT. Table 1's extracted layout is ambiguous.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for additional task results were not extracted: MLP-N/MLP-X on MNIST, ResNet-20/32 on CIFAR-100, ImageNet CNN-10, few-shot recognition, GCN, PointNet, S-OPT, large categorical training, and PE-OPT ablations. These report task-level OPT comparisons but are outside the core test-error landscape and OPT-vs-baseline examples selected here. Relevant results appear in Tables 6–13 and 19–20.

untested.parts: Matched random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold. S-OPT sampling dimensions and PE-OPT parameter counts change parameterization, not network width.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers under comparable conditions, including local connectivity and transferred initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets. Different optimizers used for different tasks supply no such comparison.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware training-error sharpness tracking measured generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples compared with equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain outside V1–V8; their states therefore cannot indicate support, absence, or reversal of a supplied version. Method-performance rows should be retained only as findings outside these versions. The paper discusses or cites related generalization ideas, but does not operationally rely on a supplied version as a tool, so T4 is inappropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and learned local connectivity.
Large- versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
